label: dam-probe-p19-decision-headroom
_why: ENGINE PROBE (user, 2026-09-28: F168's "the AI takes every visible decision in one pass" is an inference - "Are you sure there can be no mean_week_to_pick parameter expressable ... How is this done with vanilla canals?"). The AI takes the SURVEY DECISION itself, vanilla canal style, instead of the quarterly driver (which is not hooked): ai_chance = 0, +10 when produced - used bureaucracy exceeds the survey's cost, x0 at war / in a diplomatic play / in default. NO survey count: `possible` requires the country's spare bureaucracy (produced - used) to exceed THIS survey's cost (user, 2026-09-28: "I think the bureaucracy cost is a sufficient gate by itself. The trick is to make it work for AI."). F168 overshot with possible = produced > cost (Britain 2,395 used -> 8,465 a week later). Paired with the other gate placement: same-day multiple takes under one and not the other tell whether possible is re-checked after each take.

_questions.Q1: Does a country's bureaucracy usage ever overshoot its production because several surveys were taken at once (same-day starts whose combined cost exceeds the headroom at the first)?
_questions.Q2: How many surveys does a major run at once, and does it keep starting new ones as the old complete (its spare bureaucracy as the only limit)?

_predictions.Q1: unknown - the point: no overshoot if possible is re-checked after each take and the survey modifier counts at once
_predictions.Q2: majors run several at once, bounded by their spare bureaucracy

_caveats: Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (landmine L30).
Probe build: techs granted, costs and surveys shrunk - no economic reading.
